registry_review.anchor_strength_and_role: SF-P147-MODERATE-SEVERE-DISTRESS is typed EXAMINATION_FINDING, which types to POSITIVE_SUPPORT and so to the PRESENTATION discriminative class in PATIENT_CLINICAL. It is an observation of the patient rather than a resource clause or a meta-judgement about the decider, so it is the kind of feature that can carry plausibility on its own. No role override is needed and none is declared.
registry_review.boolean_semantics: Verified independently against the frozen enrichment rather than against the supply layer's summary: the correctness tree is ANY_OF(SF-P147-ABRUPT-ONSET-NO-PRODROME, SF-P147-FOCAL-ASYMMETRIC-FINDINGS). SF-P147-MODERATE-SEVERE-DISTRESS is not a disjunct of it, so the anchor cannot complete the correctness signature.
registry_review.categorical_exclusion_risk: NONE. The anchor adds no category and does not move the candidate's concept category, so CS2-5 sees the same option-set shape.
registry_review.learner_decision_relevance: QGEN-GEN-PED-T01 is the most-likely-diagnosis decision in a wheezing infant, which is the decision the cited differential is a differential for.
registry_review.medical_correctness: Escalating work of breathing in an infant with a first wheeze is a recognised trigger for widening the differential to include aspiration. CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL names severe respiratory distress as exactly such an atypical presentation and CLM-R2-PED-DDX-TABLE contains foreign body aspiration. Both were reread in full for this review.
registry_review.minimality_note: The relation is needed because without it CS2-6 refuses this candidate: its frozen anchor set equals its correctness conditions exactly. That is a structural defect in the frozen anchor derivation, not a yield argument.
registry_review.second_key_risk: NONE, on the Boolean check above.
registry_review.source_support: CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL and CLM-R2-PED-DDX-TABLE, both VERIFIED_COMPLETE in the R2 evidence packet, both reread verbatim.
registry_review.state_semantics: Required state PRESENT. Where the stem is silent the feature is UNKNOWN and the relation does not fire; nothing here reads silence as absence.

context.s4_limb_c: The candidate's correctness conditions are ANY_OF(not improving as expected, severity raising bacterial concern, focal consolidation). registry_review.anchor_strength_and_role: Same feature and same typing as the aspiration relation: EXAMINATION_FINDING to POSITIVE_SUPPORT, inside ANCHOR_CLASSES.
registry_review.boolean_semantics: The correctness tree is ANY_OF(SF-P147-FAILING-TO-IMPROVE, SF-P147-SEVERE-OR-BACTERIAL-CONCERN, SF-P147-FOCAL-ASYMMETRIC-FINDINGS). The anchor is not among the three.
registry_review.learner_decision_relevance: Same decision and same cited differential.
registry_review.medical_correctness: Bacterial pneumonia is the standard alternative considered in an infant with a lower respiratory illness and rising work of breathing, and it sits in the same cited differential table.
registry_review.minimality_note: Needed for the same structural reason: this candidate's frozen anchor set is a subset of its own correctness disjuncts.
registry_review.second_key_risk: NONE by the gate, and this is the one relation in the set where the review had to work. The objection is that CLM-GEN-PED-INV-01 speaks of 'severity suggesting an alternative such as bacterial pneumonia', so a reader could collapse escalating work of breathing into SF-P147-SEVERE-OR-BACTERIAL-CONCERN, which IS a disjunct. The frozen vocabulary keeps them apart and the distinction is real: SF-P147-MODERATE-SEVERE-DISTRESS is an observation of respiratory effort, while SF-P147-SEVERE-OR-BACTERIAL-CONCERN is the judgement that a specific bacterial possibility has been raised, and the frozen G2-PED-01 reading already types the latter as SEVERITY_FEATURE on CLM-R2-PED-CXR-INDICATION for that reason. A stem that states the observation and not the judgement leaves the disjunct UNKNOWN, so the tree is INDETERMINATE and not SATISFIED. The relation is approved on that reading and the objection is recorded rather than dismissed.
registry_review.state_semantics: Required state PRESENT; silence stays UNKNOWN.

registry_review.reason: SU-P-147 has no feature for noisy breathing since birth, a positional or biphasic character, or a chronic course, so this candidate cannot state a correctness condition at all. Registering three new features to hold them is a vocabulary extension, which needs its own evidence packet and its own authorization; this registry does not grow the frozen vocabulary. no_new_discovery: Every proposal here was discovered by the already-run frozen-five supply wave. No further supply wave was run, no competitor was discovered and no evidence was acquired.

review_independence.stated_limit: R-REGISTRY-1 is a separate reasoning pass by the same model instance rather than a separate agent, which is a weaker form of independence than the three fresh reviewers of the contrast-first pilot. It is stated rather than glossed. Every load-bearing claim was checked against the frozen artifact rather than against the supply layer's summary of it: the correctness trees were reread from the frozen enrichments, the role override from the frozen V2 readings, and all six cited claims from the R2 and R4 evidence packets.
review_independence.what_is_new: A registry-level review, R-REGISTRY-1, on the questions a registry has to answer and the supply wave never asked: does the feature exist, is the anchor role inside ANCHOR_CLASSES or does it need a cited override, is the relation a duplicate of one already registered, and does it survive the minimality rule.
review_independence.what_is_reused: The supply wave's own clinical review, by R-SUPPLY-A/B/C, on medical plausibility, learner-decision match, response class, granularity, Boolean reading and second-key risk. It is recorded per extension and not re-litigated.
